```bash
f='CHANGELOG.md'; s=open(f).read()
b="### Fixed\n\n"; i=s.index("## [Unreleased]"); k=s.index(b,i)+len(b)
s=s[:k]+("- Development builds derive `--version` only from `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags, so an unrelated tag in\n"
         "  the repository can no longer be reported as the CLI version.\n")+s[k:]
open(f,'w').write(s)
```

```text
package gitx_test

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx/gittest"
)

func TestUncommitAndRecommitReuseFullMessage(t *testing.T) {
	isolateTransactions(t)
	r := gittest.New(t)
	r.Write("feature.txt", "feature\n")
	r.Git("add", "feature.txt")
	r.Git("commit", "-m", "feat: subject", "-m", "body line one\nbody line two")
	old := r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
	parent := r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD^")

	receipt, err := gitx.Uncommit(context.Background(), r.Root, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if receipt.OldOID != old || receipt.Parent != parent || r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD") != parent {
		t.Fatalf("receipt/head = %+v head=%s", receipt, r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD"))
	}
	status, err := gitx.StatusOf(context.Background(), r.Root)
```

Add and run the REBASE_HEAD regression test

```bash
cd /Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli
cat >> internal/gitx/transactions_test.go <<'GO'

// Git leaves REBASE_HEAD behind after a rebase completes. Treating that file as
// evidence of an in-progress operation permanently blocked retirement for every
// worktree that had ever been rebased, so it must not count.
func TestInProgressIgnoresRebaseHeadLeftByACompletedRebase(t *testing.T) {
	isolateTransactions(t)
	r := gittest.New(t)
	r.Write("feature.txt", "feature\n")
	r.Git("add", "feature.txt")
	r.Git("commit", "-m", "feat: work")

	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(r.Root, ".git", "REBASE_HEAD"),
		[]byte(r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD")+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(r.Root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if active {
		t.Fatalf("leftover REBASE_HEAD reported %q as in progress", operation)
	}

	// A real interrupted rebase still has to be reported.
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(r.Root, ".git", "rebase-merge"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	operation, active, err = gitx.InProgress(r.Root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !active || operation != "rebase-merge" {
		t.Fatalf("in-progress rebase = %q/%v", operation, active)
	}
}
GO
gofmt -w internal/gitx/transactions_test.go
go test ./internal/gitx -run 'TestInProgressIgnoresRebaseHeadLeftByACompletedRebase' -v 2>&1 | grep -E '^(=== RUN|--- |ok|FAIL)'
```

```text
func newArtifactCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "artifact", Short: "Inspect and finalize armed agent artifacts"}
	cmd.AddCommand(newArtifactFinalizeCmd(app), newArtifactListCmd(app), newArtifactObserveCmd(app))
	return cmd
}

func newArtifactFinalizeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	var (
		intentID      string
		runID         string
		settle        time.Duration
		ifPending     bool
		writerStopped bool
	)
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "finalize",
		Short: "Commit one exact stable transcript after its writer exits",
		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			store := artifactStore(app)
			resolvedRunID := firstNonEmpty(runID, os.Getenv("DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID"))
			if ifPending && intentID == "" {
				if _, err := store.FindByRunID(resolvedRunID); errors.Is(err, artifact.ErrIntentNotFound) {
					return nil
				} else if err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
			service := &artifact.Service{Store: store, ScanStaged: scanAgentArtifacts}
			intent, err := service.Finalize(ctxOf(), artifact.FinalizeRequest{
				IntentID: intentID, RunID: resolvedRunID, Settle: settle, WriterStopped: writerStopped,
			})
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "FINALIZED %s\n", intent.ID)
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   commit      %s\n", shortOID(intent.ArtifactCommit))
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   transcript  %s\n", config.Contract(intent.TranscriptPath))
			return nil
		},
	}
	f := cmd.Flags()
	f.StringVar(&intentID, "intent", "", "artifact intent id")
	f.StringVar(&runID, "run-id", "", "outer wrapper run id")
	f.DurationVar(&settle, "settle", 500*time.Millisecond, "required transcript stability interval")
	f.BoolVar(&ifPending, "if-pending", false, "silently succeed when no armed intent matches the run id")
	f.BoolVar(&writerStopped, "writer-stopped", false, "confirm the outer agent wrapper has returned before finalization")
	return cmd
}

func newArtifactListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "list",
		Short: "List pending and finalized artifact intents",
		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			intents, err := artifactStore(app).List()
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			table := NewTable("INTENT", "STATUS", "SESSION", "BRANCH", "COMMIT")
			for _, intent := range intents {
				table.Add(intent.ID, string(intent.Status), intent.Provider+":"+shortOID(intent.SessionID),
					intent.Branch, shortOID(intent.ArtifactCommit))
			}
			table.Render(app.Out)
			return nil
		},
	}
}

=== ensureArtifactsFinalized ===
func ensureArtifactsFinalized(app *App, worktree string) error {
	store := artifactStore(app)
	intents, err := store.List()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(worktree)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, intent := range intents {
		intentPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
		if canonicalErr != nil || intentPath != canonical {
			continue
		}
		if intent.Status != artifact.Finalized {
			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent for %s is %s; finalize it before integration or retirement", config.Contract(worktree), intent.Status)
		}
		reconciled, reconcileErr := (&artifact.Service{Store: store}).Finalize(context.Background(), artifact.FinalizeRequest{IntentID: intent.ID})
		if reconcileErr != nil {
			return reconcileErr
		}
		intent = *reconciled
		if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" || !artifactCommitReachable(intent) {
			return fmt.Errorf("artifact commit for %s is no longer reachable; restore or re-finalize intent %s before integration or retirement",
				config.Contract(worktree), intent.ID)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```bash
		Short: "Abandon an intent that can never be finalized",
		Long: `Record that an armed handoff will never produce a commit.

An intent whose transcript was never written, or whose HEAD no longer exists
after a rebase, can never be finalized, and until now it blocked integration and
retirement forever with no way out except editing dev state by hand.

Discarding commits nothing and recovers nothing. It states, durably, that the

				return err
			}
			switch intent.Status {
			case artifact.Discarded:

				return nil
			case artifact.Finalized:

			case artifact.Armed, artifact.Finalizing:
```

```text
func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
	t.Helper()
	home := t.TempDir()
	scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
	wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
	// real use rather than via an absolute path.
	r := gittest.New(t)
	dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
	if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r.Root = dest

	// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
	t.Setenv("HOME", home)
	t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
	gitConfig := "[user]\n\temail = dev@example.test\n\tname = dev test\n[init]\n\tdefaultBranch = main\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(home, ".gitconfig"), []byte(gitConfig), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
	cfg := "" +
		"[paths]\n" +
		"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
		"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
		"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
		"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
		"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
		"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
		"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
}

// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
	h.t.Helper()
	var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
	root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
	root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))
	err := root.Execute()
	return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
}

func (h *harness) mustRun(args ...string) string {
	h.t.Helper()
	out, errOut, err := h.run(args...)
	if err != nil {
		h.t.Fatalf("dev %s: %v\nstderr: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, errOut)
	}
	return out
}
```

```bash
cd /Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli

// An intent whose transcript was never written, or whose HEAD is gone after a
// rebase, can never be finalized. Before `dev artifact discard` existed it
// blocked integration and retirement forever with no tool-mediated way out.
func TestArtifactDiscardUnblocksAnIntentThatCanNeverFinalize(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	intentDir := filepath.Join(h.home, "state", "artifact-intents", "v1")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(intentDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	record := `{"schema_version":1,"id":"intent-deadbeef","run_id":"codex-run","provider":"codex",` +
		`"session_id":"11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555","repo_path":"` + h.repo.Root + `",` +
		`"git_common_dir":"` + filepath.Join(h.repo.Root, ".git") + `","worktree_path":"` + h.repo.Root + `",` +
		`"branch":"feat/gone","head":"0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","status":"failed"}`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(intentDir, "intent-deadbeef.json"), []byte(record), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Without --yes and without a TTY the loss must not happen silently.
	if _, _, err := h.run("artifact", "discard", "intent-deadbeef"); err == nil ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "pass --yes") {
		t.Fatalf("unconfirmed discard = %v", err)
	}
	if out := h.mustRun("artifact", "list"); !strings.Contains(out, "failed") {
		t.Fatalf("refused discard changed the intent:\n%s", out)
	}

	out := h.mustRun("artifact", "discard", "intent-deadbeef", "--yes")
	for _, want := range []string{"DISCARDING", "codex:", "feat/gone", "cannot be undone", "DISCARDED"} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Errorf("discard output missing %q:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
	if listed := h.mustRun("artifact", "list"); !strings.Contains(listed, "discarded") {
		t.Fatalf("intent was not recorded as discarded:\n%s", listed)
	}
	// Re-running is a no-op rather than an error, so cleanup scripts are safe.
	if again := h.mustRun("artifact", "discard", "intent-deadbeef", "--yes"); !strings.Contains(again, "already discarded") {
		t.Fatalf("second discard = %q", again)
	}
}

// An armed intent still has a live path to preserving its transcript, so
// discarding it must be refused rather than offered as a shortcut.
func TestArtifactDiscardRefusesAnArmedIntent(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	intentDir := filepath.Join(h.home, "state", "artifact-intents", "v1")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(intentDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	record := `{"schema_version":1,"id":"intent-armed01","run_id":"codex-run","provider":"codex",` +
		`"session_id":"11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555","repo_path":"` + h.repo.Root + `",` +
		`"git_common_dir":"` + filepath.Join(h.repo.Root, ".git") + `","worktree_path":"` + h.repo.Root + `",` +
		`"branch":"feat/live","head":"0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","status":"armed"}`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(intentDir, "intent-armed01.json"), []byte(record), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, _, err := h.run("artifact", "discard", "intent-armed01", "--yes")
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "finalize") {
		t.Fatalf("discarding an armed intent = %v", err)
	}
}
GO
```

```bash
old='''	// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
	if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {'''
new='''	// A branch-backed task whose branch git no longer has is dead: the branch
	// was deleted after integration, so the record holds intent for work that
	// no longer exists anywhere. It cannot be finished, resumed, or retired,
	// because every one of those paths resolves the branch first.
	if t.WorktreePath == "" && t.Branch != "" && t.RepoPath != "" &&
		t.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeDirect && !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, t.Branch) {
		out = append(out, suggestion{
			row:    r,
			reason: fmt.Sprintf("branch %s no longer exists", t.Branch),
			action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
			apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
		})
		return out
	}

	// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
	if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {'''
assert s.count(old)==1
open(f,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
print("added dead-branch drift detection")
```

```bash
// A branch-backed task whose branch was deleted after integration can be
// finished by no path at all: done, resume and retire all resolve the branch
// first. Sweep must offer to reap the record instead of leaving it forever.
func TestSweepReapsATaskWhoseBranchIsGone(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "landed", "--branch", "feat/landed", "--base", "main")
	wtPath := filepath.Join(h.wtRoot, "demo", "feat-landed")
	h.mustRun("wt", "rm", "feat/landed", "--repo", "demo")
	if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("worktree still present: %v", err)
	}
	h.repo.Git("branch", "-D", "feat/landed")

	report := h.mustRun("sweep")
	if !strings.Contains(report, "branch feat/landed no longer exists") ||
		!strings.Contains(report, "reap the task entry") {
		t.Fatalf("sweep did not report the dead branch:\n%s", report)
	}
	// Report-only until --apply, like every other suggestion.
	if listed := h.mustRun("ls", "--json"); !strings.Contains(listed, "landed") {
		t.Fatalf("report-only sweep removed the task:\n%s", listed)
	}

	h.mustRun("sweep", "--apply", "--yes")
	if listed := h.mustRun("ls", "--json"); strings.Contains(listed, "feat/landed") {
		t.Fatalf("task was not reaped:\n%s", listed)
	}
}
GO
```

```text
`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:

- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
  recorded worktree git no longer knows about.
- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
  pushed, that could go cold.

It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
sidebar, and usually the larger half.

From the canonical default-branch checkout, `--merged-worktrees` switches to a
focused audit of tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are
already contained in main. It suppresses unrelated stale-task/session noise so
the result can be presented directly for cleanup approval. Dirty trees, active
Git operations, pending artifact
intents, active/mixed runtimes, detached heads and unmerged branches are
reported as blockers. Safe candidates still require `--apply` and individual
confirmation; `--delete-branches` is a separate opt-in.

Agent workflow: show the report to the user as a concrete QA prompt, naming the
exact candidate paths and whether branches would be retained. Only after the
user approves that set may the agent add `--apply --yes`.

`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. DONE
```

## Landed — 5 branches, rebase + `--ff-only`, linear history preserved

| Branch | What it brought | Docs |

| `feat/attach-session` | interactive `dev done` wizard, semantic `--color` | backfilled EN+zh-TW |

| `feat/agent-safe-retirement` | `dev retire`, `dev prepare`/`artifact`, `sweep --merged-worktrees` | **new** bilingual guide |
| `feat/dev-journal` | `dev journal` + `dev summary` | wired nav translations |

Every branch passed `gofmt`/`vet`/`go test -race`/`skill-check` and the full strict docs chain **before** its merge. `make all` + `make e2e` pass on the result. 29 commits ahead of `origin/main`, zero merge commits.

**I rescued `feat/agent-skill-manager` first** — its branch tip was already in `main` and a complete feature (`internal/agentskill`, 591+212 lines, its own docs) was sitting uncommitted.

## Cleanup

All 5 worktrees retired via `dev retire` / `dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply`, all 10 merged branches deleted, both orphan shells removed, dead task record reaped. Herdr: `dev retire` closed 4 workspaces; I closed the stale `azure-devops-remote-repo` one manually and saved that step to memory.

**Salvage:** the two orphan directories held *longer, final* transcripts than what was committed. I restored the complete versions before deleting the shells rather than assuming they were duplicates.

## Four real bugs found by doing this

1. **`REBASE_HEAD` false positive** — git leaves it after a *completed* rebase, so `InProgress` permanently blocked retirement for any rebased worktree. This blocked the tool on its own workflow.
2. **`dev artifact discard` didn't exist** — an intent whose transcript was never written could never be finalized, blocking `done`/`park --cold`/`wt rm`/`retire` forever with no escape but hand-editing state. Added it; refuses `armed` intents.
3. **Dead-branch tasks were unreapable** — `done`/`resume`/`retire` all resolve the branch first. `dev sweep` now detects and offers to reap them.
4. **`git describe --tags`** matched any tag, so my backup tags became the reported CLI version. Restricted to `v[0-9]*`.

Also extracted `internal/lockx` — `gitx` needed the catalog's lock, which would have cycled `gitx → catalog → forge → gitx`.

## Two things to flag

- **`main` is 29 commits ahead of `origin/main` and unpushed** — I didn't push; say the word.
- **`TestPosixShellWrapperFallsBackFromStaleTMPDIR/zsh` is flaky** under parallel load (spawns a real `zsh`). It failed once early on, passes consistently otherwise. Not fixed — tell me if you want it hardened.
- Backup tags (`backup/*`, `rescue/*`) are still in place as an escape hatch; they no longer affect `--version`. Delete when you're satisfied.
- I left the `agent-skills` dead task alone — different repo, and its `next` note says "review and publish upstream exact selectors", so that's your call.

```text
1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"io"
6		"os"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	const (
11		colorAuto   = "auto"
12		colorAlways = "always"
13		colorNever  = "never"
14	
15		ansiReset   = "\x1b[0m"
16		ansiBold    = "\x1b[1m"
17		ansiDim     = "\x1b[2m"
18		ansiRed     = "\x1b[31m"
19		ansiGreen   = "\x1b[32m"
20		ansiYellow  = "\x1b[33m"
21		ansiMagenta = "\x1b[35m"
22		ansiCyan    = "\x1b[36m"
23	)
24	
25	type cliStyle struct {
26		enabled bool
27	}
28	
29	func validateColorMode(mode string) error {
30		switch mode {
31		case "", colorAuto, colorAlways, colorNever:
32			return nil
33		default:
34			return fmt.Errorf("invalid --color value %q: use auto, always, or never", mode)
35		}
36	}
37	
38	func styleForWriter(w io.Writer, mode string) cliStyle {
39		switch mode {
40		case colorAlways:
41			return cliStyle{enabled: true}
42		case colorNever:
43			return cliStyle{}
44		}
45		if os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" || os.Getenv("TERM") == "dumb" {
46			return cliStyle{}
47		}
48		f, ok := w.(*os.File)
49		if !ok {
50			return cliStyle{}
51		}
52		info, err := f.Stat()
53		return cliStyle{enabled: err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice != 0}
54	}
55	
56	func (s cliStyle) paint(code, text string) string {
57		if !s.enabled || text == "" {
58			return text
59		}
60		return code + text + ansiReset
61	}
62	
63	func (s cliStyle) title(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
64	func (s cliStyle) header(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
65	func (s cliStyle) prompt(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
66	func (s cliStyle) label(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
67	func (s cliStyle) dim(text string) string     { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
68	func (s cliStyle) success(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiGreen, text) }
69	func (s cliStyle) warning(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiYellow, text) }
70	func (s cliStyle) danger(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiRed, text) }
71	func (s cliStyle) review(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiMagenta, text) }
72	
73	func (s cliStyle) taskState(text string) string {
74		return s.taskStateFor(text, text)
75	}
76	
77	func (s cliStyle) taskStateFor(state, text string) string {
78		switch strings.ToLower(state) {
79		case "hot", "done":
80			return s.success(text)
81		case "warm", "cold", "parked":
82			return s.warning(text)
83		default:
84			return text
85		}
86	}
87	
88	func colorModeFromArgs(args []string) string {
89		for i, arg := range args {
90			if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--color=") {
91				return strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--color=")
92			}
93			if arg == "--color" && i+1 < len(args) {
94				return args[i+1]
95			}
96		}
97		return colorAuto
98	}
99	
100	func (s cliStyle) git(text string) string {
101		lower := strings.ToLower(text)
102		switch {
103		case text == "—", text == "", lower == "local":
104			return s.dim(text)
105		case lower == "clean":
106			return s.success(text)
107		case text == "?", strings.Contains(text, "="), strings.Contains(lower, "conflict"), strings.Contains(lower, "error"):
108			return s.danger(text)
109		case strings.Contains(lower, "dirty"), strings.Contains(lower, "ahead"),
110			strings.Contains(lower, "behind"), strings.Contains(lower, "no checkout"),
111			strings.Contains(lower, "prunable"), strings.Contains(lower, "locked"),
112			strings.Contains(text, "!"), strings.Contains(text, "?"):
113			return s.warning(text)
114		default:
115			return text
116		}
117	}
118	
119	func (a *App) outStyle() cliStyle { return styleForWriter(a.Out, a.colorMode) }
120	func (a *App) errStyle() cliStyle { return styleForWriter(a.Err, a.colorMode) }
121	
122	func (a *App) newTable(header ...string) *Table {
123		return &Table{head: header, style: a.outStyle()}
124	}
125	
126	func renderCobraHelp(body string, style cliStyle) string {
127		if !style.enabled {
128			return body
129		}
130		headings := map[string]bool{
131			"Usage:": true, "Aliases:": true, "Examples:": true,
132			"Available Commands:": true, "Flags:": true, "Global Flags:": true,
133			"Additional help topics:": true,
134		}
135		lines := strings.Split(body, "\n")
136		for i, line := range lines {
137			if headings[strings.TrimSpace(line)] {
138				lines[i] = style.header(line)
139			}
140		}
141		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
142	}
```

```text
1	package cli

15	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags. VersionFromBuild also recovers a
16	// module version for `go install ...@version` builds.
17	var Version = "dev"
18	
19	func versionFromBuild() string {
20		if Version != "dev" {
21			return Version
22		}
23		if info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo(); ok && info.Main.Version != "" && info.Main.Version != "(devel)" {
24			return info.Main.Version
25		}
26		return Version
27	}
28	
29	const workflowTLDR = `TL;DR: default managed-task loop
30	
31	  dev start --> HOT: work / commit / test
32	                  ^               |
33	                  |  dev resume   |  dev park --next "..."
34	                  +------ WARM <--+
35	                  |
36	                  +-- direct:          dev done      --> DONE
37	                  +-- branch/worktree: dev done --ff --> DONE
38	                  +-- branch/worktree: dev done --pr --> push / review handoff
39	                                                        |
40	                          feedback --> resume if parked --> work
41	
42	  DONE --> dev sweep (report) --> dev sweep --apply (reap) --> next task
43	  Remote merge detection and cleanup are not automatic; verify integration first.`
44	
45	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
46	
47	It exists to keep four things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
48	
49	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
50	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
51	  herdr / tmux / zellij
52	                  a per-host live runtime
53	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
54	
55	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
56	human intent Git cannot answer — task state/owner/next action and asset identity,
57	tags, notes and experiment lifecycle — so closing a runtime session or moving a
58	Try never means losing the thread. Transient pane data is not persisted.
59	
60	` + workflowTLDR
61	
62	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
63	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
64		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
65	}
66	
67	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
68	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
69	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
70	// descriptors.
71	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
72		app := &App{In: os.Stdin, Out: out, Err: errOut}
73	
74		root := &cobra.Command{
75			Use:           "dev",
76			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
77			Long:          rootLong,
78			Version:       versionFromBuild(),
79			SilenceUsage:  true,
80			SilenceErrors: true,
81			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
82			// exists to answer.
83			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
84				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
85					out, err := skill.Render()
86					if err != nil {
87						return err
88					}
89					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
90					return nil
91				}
92				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
93				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
94				if interactive() {
95					return runTUI(app)
96				}
97				return runList(app, listOptions{})
98			},
99			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
100				if err := validateColorMode(app.colorMode); err != nil {
101					return err
102				}
103				if completionInvocation(cmd) {
104					return nil
105				}
106				return app.Load()
107			},
108		}
109	
110		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
111		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
112		pf.StringVar(&app.remotesPath, "remotes", "", "path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)")
113		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none")
114		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
115		pf.BoolVar(&app.allowSharedCheckout, "allow-shared-checkout", false,
116			"allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent")
117		pf.StringVar(&app.colorMode, "color", colorAuto, "colorize human output: auto, always or never")
118		registerFlagCompletion(root, "runtime", runtimeCompletions())
119		registerFlagCompletion(root, "color", fixedCompletions(colorAuto, colorAlways, colorNever))
120	
121		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
122		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
123		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
124	
125		root.AddCommand(
126			newListCmd(app),
127			newTUICmd(app),
128			newStatusCmd(app),
129			newStartCmd(app),
130			newParkCmd(app),
131			newResumeCmd(app),
132			newPrepareCmd(app),
133			newDoneCmd(app),
134			newRetireCmd(app),
135			newArtifactCmd(app),
136			newSweepCmd(app),
137			newAdoptCmd(app),
138			newBootstrapCmd(app),
139			newWorktreeCmd(app),
140			newRepoCmd(app),
141			newFleetCmd(app),
142			newGitCmd(app),
143			newGitignoreCmd(app),
144			newTryCmd(app),
145			newTriesCmd(app),
146			newGraduateCmd(app),
147			newJournalCmd(app),
148			newSummaryCmd(app),
149			newStatsCmd(app),
150			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
151			newSkillCmd(app),
152			newDoctorCmd(app),
153			newShellInitCmd(app),
154			newConfigCmd(app),
155			newCacheCmd(app),
156			newNoteCmd(app),
157			newEditCmd(app),
158		)
159		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
160		root.SetOut(out)
161		root.SetErr(errOut)
162		defaultHelp := root.HelpFunc()
163		root.SetHelpFunc(func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
164			var buf bytes.Buffer
165			previous := cmd.OutOrStdout()
166			cmd.SetOut(&buf)
167			defaultHelp(cmd, args)
168			cmd.SetOut(previous)
169			fmt.Fprint(previous, renderCobraHelp(buf.String(), app.outStyle()))
170		})
171		return root
172	}
173	
174	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
175	func Execute() int {
176		root := NewRootCommand()
177		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
178			msg := err.Error()
179			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
180			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
181				style := styleForWriter(os.Stderr, colorModeFromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
182				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, style.danger("dev:")+" "+msg)
183			}
184			return 1
185		}
186		return 0
```

 `./internal/help/help.go`

```text
1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
100
```

```text
130			}

147	func validatePasswordSource(host string, source PasswordSource) error {
148		kind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(source.Type))
149		if kind == "" {
150			kind = "none"
151		}
152		switch kind {
153		case "none", "prompt":
154			return nil
155		case "plain":

157				return fmt.Errorf("host %q plain ssh_login_password_source requires value", host)
158			}
159		case "bitwarden":

161				return fmt.Errorf("host %q bitwarden ssh_login_password_source requires item", host)
162			}
163		default:
164			return fmt.Errorf("host %q ssh_login_password_source.type %q: want none, plain, prompt or bitwarden", host, source.Type)
165		}
166		return nil
167	}

187	func CheckPrivateMode(path string, cfg Config) error {
188		needsPrivate := false
```

```text
276	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
277	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
278	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
279	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
280		cfg := Default()
281		if path == "" {
282			path = ConfigFile()
283		}
284		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
285		switch {
286		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
287			return cfg, nil
288		case err != nil:
289			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
290		}
291		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
292			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
293			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
294			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
295		}
296		cfg.Source = path
297		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
298	}

300	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
301	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
302	func (c Config) Validate() error {
303		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
304		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "zellij", "none":
305		default:
306			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux, zellij or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
307		}
308		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
309			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
310		}
311		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
312			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
313		}
314		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
315		case "", "flat", "preserve":
316		default:
317			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
318		}
319		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
320			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
321		}
322		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
323			return fmt.Errorf("deprecated forge.remote_limit must be zero or positive")
324		}
325		seenAzureTargets := map[string]bool{}
326		for i, target := range c.Forge.AzureDevOps {
327			organization := strings.TrimSpace(target.Organization)
328			project := strings.TrimSpace(target.Project)
329			if !validAzureDevOpsOrganization(organization) {
330				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].organization %q: want an Azure DevOps Services URL like https://dev.azure.com/acme", i, target.Organization)
331			}
332			if project == "" {
333				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].project must not be empty", i)
334			}
335			key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimRight(organization, "/") + "/" + project)
336			if seenAzureTargets[key] {
337				return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d] duplicates organization/project %s / %s", i, organization, project)
338			}
339			seenAzureTargets[key] = true
340		}
341		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
342			switch v {
343			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
344				return true
345			}
346			return false
347		}
348		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
349			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
350		}
351		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
352			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
353				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
354					ecosystem, strategy)
355			}
356		}
357		validColumns := map[string]bool{
358			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "remote": true, "size": true, "live": true,
359			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true, "notes": true,
360			"category": true, "path": true,
361		}
362		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
363			if !validColumns[column] {
364				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
365			}
366		}
367		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
368		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "size", "tasks":
369		default:
370			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git, size or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
371		}
372		seen := map[string]string{}
373		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
374			switch {
375			case t.Key == "":
376				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
377			case t.Run == "":
378				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
379			}
380			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
381				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
382					i, t.Key, binding)
383			}
384			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
385				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
386			}
387			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
388		}
389		return nil
390	}
391	
392	func validAzureDevOpsOrganization(raw string) bool {
393		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
394		if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil ||
395			u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.Port() != "" {
396			return false
397		}
398		host := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
399		segments := strings.FieldsFunc(u.Path, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' })
400		switch {
401		case host == "dev.azure.com":
402			return len(segments) == 1
403		case strings.HasSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com"):
404			organization := strings.TrimSuffix(host, ".visualstudio.com")
405			return organization != "" && organization != "vs-ssh" && len(segments) == 0
406		default:
407			return false
408		}
409	}

462	// DiscoveryRoots returns exact repositories first, followed by recursive scan
463	// roots. repo.Discover recognises when a supplied root is itself a repository.
464	func (c Config) DiscoveryRoots() []string {
465		seen := map[string]bool{}
466		out := make([]string, 0, len(c.Paths.RepoPaths)+len(c.Paths.ScanRoots))
467		for _, roots := range [][]string{c.RepoPaths(), c.ScanRoots()} {
468			for _, root := range roots {
469				clean := filepath.Clean(root)
470				if clean == "" || seen[clean] {
471					continue
472				}
473				seen[clean] = true
474				out = append(out, clean)
475			}
476		}
477		return out
478	}

491		rendered, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, v)
492		if err != nil {
493			return "", err
494		}
495		return Expand(rendered), nil
496	}
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}
```

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession reserves a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"). The
117		// production start/park/resume flow does not yet capture or attach it.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a Herdr
120		// workspace id). RuntimeName records which backend owns that opaque handle.
121		// Both are advisory and must be revalidated against live checkout coverage.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123		RuntimeName   string `toml:"runtime_name"`
124	
125		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
126		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
127	}
128	
129	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
130	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
131	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
132	// semantics and must be explicit.
133	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
134		if t.Mode != "" {
135			return t.Mode
136		}
137		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
138			return ModeWorktree
139		}
140		return ModeBranch
141	}
142	
143	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
144	func (t Task) Title() string {
145		if t.Name != "" {
146			return t.Name
147		}
148		return t.Branch
149	}
150	
151	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
152	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
153	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
154	
155	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
156	func (t Task) Validate() error {
157		switch {
158		case t.Repo == "":
159			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
160		case t.Branch == "":
161			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
162		case t.RepoPath == "":
163			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
164		}
165		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
166			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
167		}
168		switch t.Mode {
169		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
170		default:
171			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
172		}
173		return nil
174	}
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"regexp"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Path templates are deliberately *not* text/template: the syntax users write
10	// in config.toml ("{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}") needs to stay
11	// readable and to fail loudly on an unknown variable rather than silently
12	// rendering "<no value>".
13	
14	var tmplVar = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:\|\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*)?\}\}`)
15	
16	// Vars is the substitution environment for a path template.
17	type Vars map[string]string
18	
19	// Render substitutes every {{var}} / {{var|filter}} occurrence in tmpl.
20	// An unknown variable or filter is an error — a typo in worktree_path should
21	// surface at create time, not as a directory literally named "{{rep}}".
22	func Render(tmpl string, vars Vars) (string, error) {
23		var firstErr error
24		out := tmplVar.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(m string) string {
25			g := tmplVar.FindStringSubmatch(m)
26			name, filter := g[1], g[2]
27			val, ok := vars[name]
28			if !ok {
29				if firstErr == nil {
30					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template variable %q in %q (known: %s)", name, tmpl, strings.Join(sortedKeys(vars), ", "))
31				}
32				return m
33			}
34			switch filter {
35			case "":
36				return val
37			case "slug":
38				return Slug(val)
39			case "lower":
40				return strings.ToLower(val)
41			case "base":
42				if i := strings.LastIndexByte(val, '/'); i >= 0 {
43					return val[i+1:]
44				}
45				return val
46			default:
47				if firstErr == nil {
48					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template filter %q in %q (known: slug, lower, base)", filter, tmpl)
49				}
50				return m
51			}
52		})
53		if firstErr != nil {
54			return "", firstErr
55		}
56		return out, nil
57	}
58	
59	var slugStrip = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
60	
61	// Slug makes a branch name safe to use as a single filesystem component:
62	// "feat/auth/oauth-refresh" becomes "feat-auth-oauth-refresh". Leading dots
63	// and dashes are trimmed so the result can never be a hidden directory or be
64	// mistaken for a flag.
65	func Slug(s string) string {
66		s = slugStrip.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
67		for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
68			s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
69		}
70		s = strings.Trim(s, "-._")
71		if s == "" {
72			return "unnamed"
73		}
74		return s
75	}
76	
77	func sortedKeys(v Vars) []string {
78		out := make([]string, 0, len(v))
79		for k := range v {
80			out = append(out, k)
81		}
82		// small map; insertion sort keeps this dependency-free
83		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
84			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
85				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
86			}
87		}
88		return out
89	}
90
```

```text
1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}
```

```text
1	package cli

3	import (

8		"strings"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/inventory"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"

16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
17		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
18	)
19	
20	// suggestion is one proposed change, with the reason and the exact effect.
21	type suggestion struct {
22		row    inventory.Row
23		action string
24		reason string
25		// apply performs the change. nil means "report only".
26		apply func() error
27	}
28	
29	type sweepRetireOptions struct {
30		closeUnknown    bool
31		assumeNoRuntime bool
32		deleteBranches  bool
33	}
34	
35	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
36		var (
37			apply           bool
38			staleDays       int
39			yes             bool
40			mergedWorktrees bool
41			baseRef         string
42			closeUnknown    bool
43			assumeNoRuntime bool
44			deleteBranches  bool
45		)
46		cmd := &cobra.Command{
47			Use:   "sweep",
48			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
49			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
50	
51	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
52	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
53	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
54	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
55			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
56			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
57				ctx := ctxOf()
58				tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
59				if err != nil {
60					return err
61				}
62				rt := app.Runtime()
63				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
64				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
65				retireOptions := sweepRetireOptions{
66					closeUnknown: closeUnknown, assumeNoRuntime: assumeNoRuntime, deleteBranches: deleteBranches,
67				}
68	
69				var sugg []suggestion
70				if mergedWorktrees {
71					merged, err := suggestMergedWorktrees(app, ctx, rows, baseRef, retireOptions)
72					if err != nil {
73						return err
74					}
75					sugg = append(sugg, merged...)
76				} else {
77					for _, r := range rows {
78						sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, r, stale, retireOptions)...)
79					}
80				}
81	
82				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
83				if !mergedWorktrees {
84					if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
85						if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
86							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
87							for _, s := range orphans {
88								dir := "—"
89								if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
90									dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])
91								}
92								fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
93							}
94							fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  → `dev start` in one of those directories to track it, or just close it.")
95						}
96					}
97				}
98	
99				if len(sugg) == 0 {
100					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — no task drift or eligible merged worktree was found.")
101					return nil
102				}
103	
104				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))
105				for _, s := range sugg {
106					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %-28s %s\n", s.row.Task.State.Icon(),
107						truncate(s.row.Task.Title(), 28), s.reason)
108					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "     → %s\n", s.action)
109				}
110	
111				if !apply {
112					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to act on these (each is confirmed individually).")
113					return nil
114				}
115	
116				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
117				for _, s := range sugg {
118					if s.apply == nil {
119						continue
120					}
121					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, s.action) {
122						continue
123					}
124					if err := s.apply(); err != nil {
125						app.warnf("%s: %v", s.row.Task.ID, err)
126						continue
127					}
128					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  done: %s\n", s.action)
129				}
130				return nil
131			},
132		}
133		f := cmd.Flags()
134		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "act on the suggestions instead of only reporting")
135		f.IntVar(&staleDays, "stale-days", 14, "days without a commit before a task counts as stale")
136		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each change")
137		f.BoolVar(&mergedWorktrees, "merged-worktrees", false, "focus on linked worktrees whose branches are contained in the main branch")
138		f.StringVar(&baseRef, "base", "", "containment base for --merged-worktrees (default: the repository default branch)")
139		f.BoolVar(&closeUnknown, "close-unknown", false, "allow external closure of unknown runtime status during retirement")
140		f.BoolVar(&assumeNoRuntime, "assume-no-runtime", false, "continue when runtime enumeration fails during retirement")
141		f.BoolVar(&deleteBranches, "delete-branches", false, "also delete contained local branches after worktree retirement")
142		return cmd
143	}
144	
145	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
146		t := r.Task
147		var out []suggestion
148	
149		switch {
150		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
151		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
152		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
153			out = append(out, suggestion{
154				row:    r,
155				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
156				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
157				apply: func() error {
158					t.State = task.Warm
159					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
160				},
161			})
162	
163		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
164		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
165		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
166			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
167			if r.Status.Dirty() {
168				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
169					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
170				break
171			}
172			if !r.Status.Synced() {
173				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
174					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
175				break
176			}
177			out = append(out, suggestion{
178				row:    r,
179				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
180				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
181				apply: func() error {
182					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
183						if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, t.WorktreePath); err != nil {
184							return err
185						}
186						if err := safeRemoveWorktree(ctx, runtimeForTask(app, t), t.RepoPath, t.WorktreePath,
187							false, false, false, 5*time.Second); err != nil {
188							return err
189						}
190						t.WorktreePath = ""
191					}
192					t.State = task.Cold
193					clearTaskRuntime(t)
194					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
195				},
196			})
197	
198		// DONE means integrated; runtime/worktree cleanup is a separate,
199		// externally coordinated retirement step.
200		case t.State == task.Done:
201			action := fmt.Sprintf("retire runtime/worktree for %s", t.ID)
202			if retireOptions.deleteBranches && t.Branch != "" && t.Branch != t.Base {
203				action += fmt.Sprintf(" and delete %s", t.Branch)
204			}
205			out = append(out, suggestion{
206				row:    r,
207				reason: "merged, cleanup pending",
208				action: action,
209				apply: func() error {
210					if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, checkoutOf(t)); err != nil {
211						return err
212					}
213					target, rt, err := retirementTargetForTask(ctx, app, t)
214					if err != nil {
215						return err
216					}
217					service := &retirement.Service{Runtime: rt, Tasks: app.Tasks}
218					_, err = service.Retire(ctx, retirement.Request{
219						Target: target,
220						Safety: retirement.Options{
221							CloseUnknown: retireOptions.closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: retireOptions.assumeNoRuntime,
222						},
223						DeleteBranch: retireOptions.deleteBranches,
224					})
225					return err
226				},
227			})
228		}
229	
230		// A branch-backed task whose branch git no longer has is dead: the branch
231		// was deleted after integration, so the record holds intent for work that
232		// no longer exists anywhere. It cannot be finished, resumed, or retired,
233		// because every one of those paths resolves the branch first.
234		noCheckout := t.WorktreePath == "" || r.WorktreeMissing
235		if noCheckout && t.Branch != "" && t.RepoPath != "" &&
236			t.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeDirect && !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, t.Branch) {
237			out = append(out, suggestion{
238				row:    r,
239				reason: fmt.Sprintf("branch %s no longer exists", t.Branch),
240				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
241				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
242			})
243			return out
244		}
245	
246		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
247		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
248			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
249			out = append(out, suggestion{
250				row:    r,
251				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
252				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
253				apply: func() error {
254					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
255						return err
256					}
257					t.WorktreePath = ""
258					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
259						t.State = task.Cold
260					}
261					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
262				},
263			})
264		}
265		return out
266	}
267	
268	func suggestMergedWorktrees(app *App, ctx context.Context, rows []inventory.Row, requestedBase string, options sweepRetireOptions) ([]suggestion, error) {
269		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, mustGetwd())
270		if err != nil {
271			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees requires a Git repository: %w", err)
272		}
273		if repository.IsLinkedWorktree {
274			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees must run from the canonical checkout, not linked worktree %s", config.Contract(repository.Root))
275		}
276		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repository.Root)
277		if err != nil {
278			return nil, err
279		}
280		base := requestedBase
281		if base == "" {
282			base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repository.Root)
283			if status.Branch != base {
284				return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees defaults to %s; switch the canonical checkout to it or pass --base explicitly", base)
285			}
286		}
287		if !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repository.Root, base) {
288			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merged-worktree base %s does not resolve to a commit", base)
289		}
290	
291		claimed := make(map[string]inventory.Row)
292		for _, row := range rows {
293			if row.Task == nil || row.Checkout == "" {
294				continue
295			}
296			canonical, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(row.Checkout)
297			if canonicalErr == nil {
298				claimed[canonical] = row
299			}
300		}
301		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, repository.Root)
302		if err != nil {
303			return nil, err
304		}
305		var suggestions []suggestion
306		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
307			if worktree.Main || worktree.Bare || worktree.Detached || worktree.Branch == "" || worktree.Branch == base {
308				continue
309			}
310			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Root, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", worktree.Branch, base); err != nil {
311				continue
312			}
313			canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
314			if err != nil {
315				continue
316			}
317			if row, ok := claimed[canonical]; ok {
318				if row.Task.State == task.Done {
319					suggestions = append(suggestions, suggestFor(app, ctx, row, 0, options)...)
320					continue
321				}
322				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base,
323					fmt.Sprintf("task is %s; verify integration with `dev done --merged` first", row.Task.State)))
324				continue
325			}
326	
327			synthetic := &task.Task{
328				ID: task.MakeID(repository.Name, worktree.Branch), Name: worktree.Branch,
329				Repo: repository.Name, RepoPath: repository.MainRoot, Branch: worktree.Branch,
330				Base: base, WorktreePath: canonical, Mode: task.ModeWorktree, State: task.Done,
331			}
332			row := inventory.Row{Task: synthetic, Checkout: canonical, CheckoutExists: true}
333			if worktree.Locked {
334				reason := "worktree is locked"
335				if worktree.LockedReason != "" {
336					reason += ": " + worktree.LockedReason
337				}
338				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, reason))
339				continue
340			}
341			if worktree.Prunable {
342				reason := "worktree registration is prunable"
343				if worktree.PrunableReason != "" {
344					reason += ": " + worktree.PrunableReason
345				}
346				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, reason))
347				continue
348			}
349			worktreeStatus, statusErr := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, canonical)
350			if statusErr != nil {
351				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, statusErr.Error()))
352				continue
353			}
354			row.Status = worktreeStatus
355			if worktreeStatus.Dirty() {
356				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base,
357					fmt.Sprintf("worktree is dirty (%s)", worktreeStatus.Breakdown())))
358				continue
359			}
360			if operation, active, operationErr := gitx.InProgress(canonical); operationErr != nil {
361				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, operationErr.Error()))
362				continue
363			} else if active {
364				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base,
365					fmt.Sprintf("Git operation %s is in progress", operation)))
366				continue
367			}
368			if artifactErr := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, canonical); artifactErr != nil {
369				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, artifactErr.Error()))
370				continue
371			}
372			inspection, inspectErr := retirement.Inspect(ctx, app.Runtime(), canonical, retirement.Options{
373				CloseUnknown: options.closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: options.assumeNoRuntime,
374			})
375			if inspectErr != nil {
376				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, inspectErr.Error()))
377				continue
378			}
379			if !inspection.Ready() {
380				suggestions = append(suggestions, mergedWorktreeBlocker(row, base, strings.Join(inspection.Blockers, "; ")))
381				continue
382			}
383	
384			branch := worktree.Branch
385			checkout := canonical
386			action := fmt.Sprintf("retire merged worktree %s", config.Contract(checkout))
387			if options.deleteBranches {
388				action += fmt.Sprintf(" and delete %s", branch)
389			}
390			suggestions = append(suggestions, suggestion{
391				row: row, reason: fmt.Sprintf("untracked worktree branch is contained in %s", base), action: action,
392				apply: func() error {
393					service := &retirement.Service{Runtime: app.Runtime()}
394					_, err := service.Retire(ctx, retirement.Request{
395						Target: retirement.Target{
396							RepoPath: repository.MainRoot, CheckoutPath: checkout,
397							Branch: branch, Base: base, LinkedWorktree: true,
398						},
399						Safety: retirement.Options{
400							CloseUnknown: options.closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: options.assumeNoRuntime,
401						},
402						DeleteBranch: options.deleteBranches,
403					})
404					return err
405				},
406			})
407		}
408		return suggestions, nil
409	}
410	
411	func mergedWorktreeBlocker(row inventory.Row, base, blocker string) suggestion {
412		return suggestion{
413			row: row, reason: fmt.Sprintf("branch is contained in %s, but retirement is blocked", base),
414			action: blocker + " — not changed automatically",
415		}
416	}
417	
418	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
419		s := app.outStyle()
420		prompt := s.prompt(action + "?")
421		lower := strings.ToLower(action)
422		if strings.Contains(lower, "delete") || strings.Contains(lower, "remove") ||
423			strings.Contains(lower, "discard") || strings.Contains(lower, "drop") {
424			prompt = s.danger(action + "?")
425		}
426		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s ", prompt, s.dim("[y/N]"))
427		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
428		if err != nil {
429			return false
430		}
431		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
432		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
433	}
```
